requirements.statement: A project hold the update takeover recorded as unverified at adoption (a releasing lease/reservation hold whose takeover_obligations row carries the unverified marker) is not reported as hold_overdue.
Such a hold is reported as its own plain finding, hold_unverified_takeover, once per project, saying it is harmless, takes no run slot, will not clear by itself and needs nothing.

The driver stops retrying settlement of a run the store records as left unverified by the takeover, on the lost-run sweep and the container recovery path: learnt from the durable record after a history_conflict (also after a restart), kept in a capped memory, with no release or account change; a conflict for any other run is still retried.
docs/troubleshooting.md Update hand-over explains in plain words the run an update left counted because its records could not be checked.
Verified takeover rows, a run still held at adoption that later goes releasing, and genuinely overdue holds behave exactly as before (never taken for unverified).

The takeover records each releasing hold it refuses as unverifiable as a durable fact in the same adoption transaction (an additive takeover_obligations row, no schema change); the fact survives journal completion, maintenance, restarts and copies of the store, and is kept and pruned under the A1 obligation retention.

The unverified-hold health finding reads live holds only through the live partial index: its work does not grow with released history (1k vs 100k released rows) and it completes within the health deadline.
